Malayalam source paragraphs GV3:P0001 to GV3:P0019
English line for line; each paragraph carries its Malayalam source number.

[GV3:P0001] Guruvani

[GV3:P0002] June 1999

[GV3:P0003] 'The space is self-luminous' - One should see the Guru in that self-luminosity. From there, one can see how vast the possibilities of that Guru are. This is the principle of the soul. Vedantins, researchers, and psychologists have nothing to do here. How many theories are there? How many postgraduate disciplines and research departments? But the one who took pride in being a theorist went his own way, and the poor man ended up nowhere. The tradition is now reaping the fruits of such actions. It has to be experienced. There is no point in blaming God for it. If the fruits of karma are to be taken back, there must be a way, a path that everyone can take together.

[GV3:P0004] Great souls like Jesus and the Prophet have done their karma for humanity across various eras, sacrificed themselves, and shown us the way. Those who are eager to reap its benefits are trying to see their doctrines in many different ways. This is the aftermath of a betrayal. Do you want to be saved from this betrayal or not? What path have you chosen for that? If any path is enough, isn't it enough to become a Christian or a Muslim - isn't it the path of the Prophet?

[GV3:P0005] What is needed is a dharma that aligns with the karma. That dharma must be sought, found, knocked upon, and opened. That is, one must seek and find a visionary who is capable of predicting what will happen until today and believe his word. Even if anyone says their word is wrong, it is not wrong. Their word is the will of God. The will of God must be respected. Grounded in that belief, one must investigate the special provisions of karma capable of sustaining the dharma of the times. By bringing the aspect of knowledge into karma, this visionary guru wipes away all sinful karma after seeing the weight of sins and virtues, transforming the soul into a virtuous one to bring it from that karma to dharma. We must see and believe in such a Guru as everything. This Guru is capable of showing the entire nature to us, the owners of karma that lies absorbed in nature. Through the glory of creation and that glory itself, this Guru will show us ourselves. The Guru will show that the Guru is present in all glories. But he is none of these. If one examines all that is said to be 'I', the inside is not many, but becomes one.

[GV3:P0006] When one comes to believe that this Guru is everything, seeing its point of origin, one sees creation and preservation. Then, this seen object is neither this nor that, nor is it the meaning of what is seen. Becoming courageous with the clarity of real meaning, it settles softly, softly. To reach this state of settling, who should the Guru you hold on to be?

[GV3:P0007] It is not easy to get such a Guru. Even if found, he will not open. To open, one must know how to knock. When one becomes courageous and settles softly upon realizing the true meaning, they have seen through the states of waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and Turiya. But these states exist in Turiya and Turiyatita. To show who stands in that state, what state must the Guru have reached? He must be someone who has gone beyond Turiya and Turiyatita. This state is what is meant when it is said that after crossing six steps and reaching there, Shiva can be seen. We could then see what Shiva was, what Shiva's karma was, what our possibilities in that karma are, and what we are going to become. We have only just begun to see it. It is later that the value of Shiva must be found. Thus we were brought here. There, the space devoid of name and form is self-luminous.

[GV3:P0008] The Guru is showing what the soul principle is. If you believe, you can find it. If you knock, it can be opened. By believing, finding, and knocking to open, all the deities of creation, preservation, and destruction have been seen. Only later is the luminous goal, which is the primordial form of all this, understood.

[GV3:P0009] The intellect of discernment will arise like ten million suns rising - this is what is said here. How can you take this? We have a difficulty in this. Because we ended up believing in all these ways. Our ancestors also lived this way. We have received this birth as a remnant of the karma done by our ancestors; and also due to the fortune of our soul. This fortune of the soul must be enlarged. Liberation must be given to the ancestors. We must take up the right of our karma and become a soul-form that shows what virtue is through dharma. Thus, one must reach a position of experience and karma worthy of making a man a Deva, a sage, an ascetic, and a liberated wise man.

[GV3:P0010] What is experiential worthiness? How far is it? All past karmas must be integrated and brought forth with a new attitude. To say it a bit more subtly, it is not that we bring it, but God makes us do it. Everything happens according to time.

[GV3:P0011] From a grain of sand to whatever things are created and destroyed in this world, everything has its own wholeness. It is with the support of these wholenesses that this world itself exists. Looking at it this way, it is clear that even wholeness cannot exist without the support of another wholeness. Humans, without knowing the mutual support of wholenesses, support here and there, seeing greatness in each thing like a frog in a well. While living in this world understanding this, a 'One' becomes necessary to stand firm on. The truth is that if one acts firmly rooted in that One, the action will be in everything. Otherwise, the action will become so empty that it won't even feel like an action was done.

[GV3:P0012] If you stretch your gaze into this atmosphere, you can see how many atoms are flashing and fading within the span of a coin. It is enough to think that we are just one among such countless atoms.

[GV3:P0013] Nothing is non-existent. If thought to be non-existent, it will lead to emptiness. All atoms have mutual access. It must be understood that this penetrating nature will reach everywhere like gas. Isn't the nature of the mind also like this? Whatever our desire is, the mind will enter into all those desires like a gas. Whether good or bad, the mind will enter that way. Some ascetics are examples of this. Through certain worship-like behaviors, they will believe and worship goddesses and gods as God. It will become a worship according to their desire. Among many such people, some will feel like showing off their prowess in it. Then the desire to apply supernatural powers (siddhis) will arise. This siddhi will be to attract people or to achieve selfish things. Whatever it is, the desire itself is the goal. One person's desire may also cause immediate harm to many.

[GV3:P0014] Since the time of creation, the world has stood as a mixture of good and bad. Thus, we, who are a mixture of good and bad, and many others like us, must think and know what this world is before performing miracles upon miracles. Otherwise, to undo the destruction caused by these miracles, one will have to constantly strive by performing more miracles. Thus, the efforts of both these groups became empty. One created, the other destroyed. No one gained anything either. This is how the so-called ascetic strives and fails. None of them did this with the desire to be bad. They slipped in their actions.

[GV3:P0015] If we do not have the innate nature to act aiming at the will of God with our minds set on the worship of God, this flaw will unknowingly take hold of us. Such flaws come to us who act in numerous external and internal matters.

[GV3:P0016] To regain the merit in karma, an era-appropriate guidance is absolutely essential. In the Kali Yuga, guidance must be given by weighing its intensity and measure. For this, there must be a clear understanding of what Kali is. The notion about Kali that people and everything else are possessed by Kali, and that it is a time when humans are ruined, unable to do good, is incorrect. We ourselves say that we have arrived on this earth according to the fruits of our past karma. If so, a little result of what was done in Treta Yuga and Dwapara Yuga will also come in this Kali. If it comes, shouldn't the good done then also come? That is, when acting in the fourth era evaluating the good and bad of the past eras, it is an absorption that reaches a liberated state that is neither good nor bad through the results of actions where the weight of sins and virtues has been balanced. There is no time like Kali where any thing can be brought forward if one works hard. That is why our ancestors, the sages, desired to be born in the Kali Yuga to attain liberation.

[GV3:P0017] Evaluating and knowing all the things that have come till today, rectifying their flaws, systematizing them according to the times, giving a form to the coming state, and striving to bring it forward is what is happening at Santhigiri. This is the knowledge given to us as Brahman.

[GV3:P0018] When systematized in an ashram nature, some differences arose from the ashram nature that has existed till today. The traditional practice of completely following the path shown by the predecessors is what is regularized here. God has entrusted us to systematize the worship methods of Vaishnavism, Shaivism, and Shaktism according to Hindu logic. This is an effort to bring a 'One' in place of all three. That is how much distance there is in the experiential worthiness of this ashram. No one else has anything to do in this.

[GV3:P0019] Guruvani

[GV3:P0020] July 1999

[GV3:P0021] Santhigiri's is the knowledge guided by God. That knowledge received here in nineteen seventy-three - a voice from the sky, a word from the light - a message from a form - behind this message is the desire that the children of the world should find peace and tranquility behind it and be able to live so. This is informed by following the word of God.

[GV3:P0022] As part of God's mercy, a lotus with two thousand four hundred and forty-four petals was shown to the disciple in a vision. Then all these petals fell off. It was only informed then that all these are those who are to arrive. Its meaning was understood through a message received several years later. These two thousand four hundred and forty-four are past gurus. All these gurus will be born in this lineage. Along with these gurus, crores of their lineage are also to be born. They all have to be born before this Kali Yuga ends. Those who work for their birth hold the position of those gurus. And then liberation. Another special provision is that the entire clan of those who create the lineage that straightaway carries this ideology will be purified. How many births will you have to take to complete this karma?

[GV3:P0023] Let me describe an illustrative vision received here. What we have seen in the world so far is nothing. There is much to be seen on a much larger scale than what has been seen. There is much to reach. It will come. A notification for that has been received. The primary lineage of this is the Santhigiri lineage.

[GV3:P0024] A stream of light is striking the earth in one or two places in Kerala. This stream of light, which guides the thinkers and religious philosophers here to the right path, is illuminating Kerala in a pattern of four, forty, four hundred. In four years, scientists will ascertain that this light exists. In forty years, it will be ascertained that this light is true and how it should be utilized. In four hundred years, the value of the theory of this light will be convinced. The language of Kerala and the dharma of India will have to be practiced by the whole world.

[GV3:P0025] People have started saying that what exists today is not enough. The people who discover this light will make public what this inadequate thing is. Along with that, a capability for karma will erupt from here so that the world understands what Santhigiri's mission is. With devotion, love, and respect mixed in, this movement, those who love this movement, and those who love this world must possess a special intelligence to be humbly accepted and sacrificed with courage in action. Understanding this and acting upon it, writers or people described as scholars, litterateurs, and ascetics and celibates who can explain the glorious deeds of visionaries must come forward. All of them have the right to absolute fulfillment. Because, the third generation of the householder - male and female - who consider the perfection of this knowledge as their life's discipline, goal, and mission by paying the full price, will be the ones who wield true efficiency in karma in any part of the world. They will be the perfect prophets of this mission, which is God's will. I say truly that every child who acts courageously for this will be praised as holy souls who impart the purity of karma essential for the eternal salvation of the world.

[GV3:P0026] God has given us the opportunity to retrieve the lost parts of the world. If it is not done properly, it will be lost again. Those parts must be grown as a support and shade for God's will. If not grown that way, or if an attempt is made to grow it by holding onto worldly justice, God will not give it again. One person must do the work of a thousand people. We have that much more work to do. Acting for one year like this will yield the result of acting for a thousand years. The thoughts and actions of you poor people will become research materials in universities within fifty years. For that, your humility and eligibility must rise to that extent. The gain from life in this ashram is very great. For that gain to happen, one must live forgetting caste and religion. Even if your beauty is destroyed, wealth is lost, or illness comes, life will not be destroyed. It is enough to be brave. If there is bravery, there is a blessed life. The life that comes like that is the greatest.

[GV3:P0027] This is not the age of Devas. Making Devas appear is not going to achieve anything either. What takes many births to achieve can be achieved in one birth in Kali. Kali is the time that came as a correction in the Rishi tradition. Kali is the time of the Shudra. The Shudra exists in all Varnas and in all times. That correction must come from the Shudra himself. For the correction in the Rishi tradition to come from the Shudra, who must he become? He must become a Rishi, a wise man, and attain liberation. He must become above all worshiped figures.

[GV3:P0028] This eligibility must come to receive the knowledge according to the will of Brahma that there has been an error in the dharma over time. Through states called disembodied voices and direct manifestations, a path of resolving karma is happening at Santhigiri, which is capable of resolving the sorrows of my twenty-nine years of life, and at the same time enabling all beings in the world to act and be made to act benevolently. The Guru path advised at Santhigiri is the greatest path of resolution that makes every human being practice the sections of dharma spanning from atoms to the absolute in the universes, bringing into them a life of dharma that removes sorrow, brings virtue through karma, and carefully guards dharma as the foundation through a life obedient to the will of Brahma. It theorizes solar system evolutions and is able not only to preserve them as theirs in karma, but it has become fully capable of bringing complete gain to the lineage.

[GV3:P0029] The Guru is appointed by the will of Brahma in accordance with the Yuga Dharma. Prophets who come for different time spans like two thousand, three thousand, five thousand years come under this Guru. The Guru is the visionary who foresees and commands what a Yuga needs and doesn't need. Only rarely in the solar system is a Guru born with the worthiness to witness such karmas. That Guru will have no aberrations. He is with the lowliest, he is with the highest, and he will not hate the rogue. Since diversity came from oneness, nothing is forbidden to such a Guru.

[GV3:P0030] An authoritative step for eternal survival throughout the world is being implemented through this ideology. Where Narayana Guru, Buddha, and Krishna left off, that is where our beginning is. We have been gifted by Brahma with a great capacity for action to function for the entire period of the Yuga Dharma as willed by Brahma, much more than what others have shown.

[GV3:P0031] Guruvani

[GV3:P0032] Guru Jayanthi Edition

[GV3:P0033] September 1999

[GV3:P0034] The Globally Radiant Path of Dharma

[GV3:P0035] Having known the good and bad through the birth we have received, we are reaching the historical truth of the long periods in which we have been born and raised under the dharmas of Kali Yuga. In this journey across lives, we have also passed by great souls who had visions for the times. But we are unable to retrieve it. Ours is a soul whose operational capacity has been lost in that way. Therefore, ours is a lifestyle of moving forward feeling happy with what is received. There is no point in living like a trapped wolf, employing our body, mind, and intellect without being able to overcome this fate.

[GV3:P0036] Kali is a time where even days, hours, and minutes are conducive to acting with awareness of the soul's operational capacity with the help of the body, which experiences waking, dreaming, and deep sleep states. It is also a time of connecting past lives, current, and future lives. If one attains firmness in present karma and achieves the elevation of dharma, this connection cannot be made. That is, if one gets trapped in contemporary theories that have gone astray, it will not be possible to move forward.

[GV3:P0037] There are many obstacles before us for this. One of them is Shaktism, Shaivism, and Vaishnavism. It may be due to the fortune of some past life that we got human birth. Thus we have had many human births before this. Unable to break away from tradition, such a person acts in various ways and loses his own fortune. As an example, for over five thousand years, great souls have come in many states and many forms of effort, yet where the Trimurti tradition has reached, the soul is spinning from there without finding a way to salvation.

[GV3:P0038] According to our belief system, the goddesses and gods we have been worshiping as deities are our God. Its succession rights belong to severe karmas ranging from ghosts to the city of vampires (Vethalanagaram). This is the biggest mistake we have inherited from our past tradition. We have not been able to realize that this is a mistake. How can we, who have degenerated to the level of having a separate god for each small caste, understand this? But we can understand. We can understand what the long historical truth of the past is by placing the soul in a suitable manner within the body, which is our accumulated karma. The status of a soul is to perceive the Yuga Dharma that has been spoken, sung, and taught about various things. Even a person who stood behind rationalism and worked firmly to acquire emptiness can qualify for this status by knowing certain things.

[GV3:P0039] When a god or goddess is worshiped and made to manifest, another will follow it. Thus, a halo of fortune of thousands of visions will come to us. To achieve this, we need a great soul capable of explaining these visions according to the times. Through that person, one must know what aspects of visions are, understand even demonic natures, and understand the part called the city of vampires before moving forward. However, we have a long history behind us of being satisfied with the gains from these ghosts, spirits, and demons, offering vows and gifts. The knowledge of our ancestors is also the same. Therefore, no one has the virtue to reclaim and act upon the dharma of the times. There is no karma that goes up to its theories. What can change this, how can it be changed - this is the subject we must think about.

[GV3:P0040] As far as we are concerned, when we move forward past the city of vampires, no matter who shows the path that reaches the karma of a Deva, the karma of a prophet, or the karma of a visionary in whichever way, an unmanageable demonic karma resides in everyone. If you look at anyone, you can see them moving forward with a kind of senseless life. We also have traditions in many forms that are unable to experience, respect, and absorb the glory and love of the Supreme Being. Without thinking about this destruction of karma, we have inherited a course of life where we cannot act upon the dharma of the times despite seeing, hearing, and knowing about it from somewhere.

[GV3:P0041] Then what is the course of life suitable for us? We must be told a traditional foundation that is lived out according to the times by conscious actions in the Turiya state, after showing visions in the waking, dreaming, and deep sleep states. This is the world-class karmic dharma. For that, one must be able to completely see (in vision) all past Kali Yugas and all Chaturyugas. One must be able to discern the truths and untruths in it. We need the foundation of knowledge brought to completion by five Gurus who reached the states of gurus across time. We, every child in all religious doctrines of the world, must get this familiarity. What is intended here is to harmoniously see the operational capacity of the past Chaturyugas and the specifics of the present and future truths of dharma. Then, we arrive at a path of knowledge where we directly see and hear what the mistakes of past times were.

[GV3:P0042] What is referred to as states is about the part that perfects Shaktism, Shaivism, and Vaishnavism. The ancestral acharyas have not been able to reach a state perfected in that way. This is also the extent of the meaning of the word 'Kala Dharma' (Dharma of the times). When looking back at the dharmas of acharyas, we can see that some great souls have practiced certain true dharmas suitable for the times. What is intended by Kala Dharma is the timely dharma that shapes their supreme love and the tri-temporal (past, present, future) natures they saw, knew, spoke, and struggled to attain. However, since we have traditionally followed a life that is out of tune with the times and lacks regularity, this timely dharma is like a reflection in the water for us.

[GV3:P0043] Knowledge is said to be like an ocean. Knowledge that reached capacity in which era? Now, by justifying and observing this, can a wise man whose soul is in distress be given guidance that integrates the four eras, acquiring the total meaning of life, seeing various wholes like the attainment of the other world, heaven, hell, or the universe, to complete it? This is a part that must be seen, known, shown, and completed. For that, a globally radiant path of truth must shine before us, showing who we each are through our past lives of mind, word, and deed. Through that, there should be a karma where the knowledge of the past and present is given correctively in parts known as vision, disembodied voice, or light. Only a visionary can give that.

[GV3:P0044] Now, who is a visionary? Is it someone who completes by singing, speaking, and writing about three periods in the Chaturyugas - presenting long lists from Puranas and epics? No. Long-term vision is the knowledge of a consciousness that stands in wisdom, devoid of birth, having seen and known the history of creation, preservation, and destruction from a grain of sand to all forms of characteristics.

[GV3:P0045] Vision is long-term vision. Seven thousand four hundred and forty-four visions is one state. Thus, when reaching a state in the nature of a visionary by seeing visions, through the person with that knowledge, determining its density--knowing how and where our mind and ideology stand in the subject we have seen, known, heard, and taken, we must start as 'one' from there.

[GV3:P0046] Narayana Guru has said in one place, "A man who crosses the boundaries of the three worlds and expands needs no other work to do," and in another place, "The lamp that shines after the triputi (knower, known, knowledge) is destroyed will not fall into the hands of a deceitful ascetic." In this section, there is a subject we must be very careful about. After the entire nature of our mind's primal karma has come into us, we can only grow according to the worthiness of the person who shows and corrects what is to come next. This is why it is commanded not to go without a Guru.

[GV3:P0047] What is said is this: We are seeing and knowing many things. In that, from ghosts, spirits, and demons to Yakshas, Gandharvas, and Kinnaras is one state. Above that, until entering the fifth state, it is a very difficult path. These states will pass through a path that is unbearable in every way and dangerous. How to retrieve these ups and downs of the mind? The karmic capability of many Chaturyugas is passing within this state. It is these temporal differences across time that are called state differences.

[GV3:P0048] It was previously mentioned that the four eras is the period that recognizes the four eras. At every level, everyone has a part called recognition--according to their own abilities. That is not what is being said here. Since it is a visionary tradition, the Guru standing in this soul-part must be someone responsible for speaking up to the light of the times. The Guru who makes the transformational phase of the soul, or the demarcation of the soul easily possible - that is the Guru standing in the soul-part.

[GV3:P0049] We have a familiarity from Puranas where some water is drawn from the sea, kept in various vessels, and we are told that it is seawater and it is pure. If we want to at least somewhat understand the dynamics of the wheel of time that changes periodically, this familiarity is not enough. It is impossible for anyone with this familiarity to reclaim the temporal divisions made of devas, asuras, and demons up to this day in the Trimurti system. Because, a force of tendencies, both good and bad, which has passed through numerous births, resides in the soul unable to recognize itself. If one starts to determine this without at least seeing and knowing some of it, the doubt will not clear. If scholars who are commentators on letters think they can clear doubts and rewrite, it won't happen. The truths of past, present, and future that have been heard, seen, and known are not subject to speculation.

[GV3:P0050] The result of effort over a long time has become the soul's karmic tendency, like a path of sacrifice. It is not easy to define and contain the familiarity of a soul with such a long time. Then, if fortunate, it might be possible to align this familiarity with the most appropriate and loving culture of a soul. Or, even if such a soul is found, it will take ages to understand it.

[GV3:P0051] A soul with numerous operational capacities crossing over ages cannot be handled by a prophet or a scientist in their simple theories. Only a Guru can handle it. Even among Gurus, only a Guru across time can do it.

[GV3:P0052] The truths of Yuga Dharma are stated variously as Satya, Treta, Dwapara, and Kali. Some historical skills will define and contain all that. When living caught up in the tendencies of the soul through life, determining what the light of each dharma is, and what its light is when that dharma reaches the state of the Trimurtis, is called historical skill. As eras pass one by one and new ones follow, it is impossible for anyone other than a Guru across time to define and contain the soul's operational capacity according to its tendencies.

[GV3:P0053] What about the knowledge of ants, cockroaches, and numerous other living beings? Vision is what defines this as a virtue. Many names and many biographies have come into the realm of knowledge. Scholars state it in their terms, and sacrificing soul-knowers state it in their terms. Those who legally practice yoga and those who do karma have their own calculations. But it is difficult for everyone to retrieve the nature of karmic differences. Because the knowledge of eras - that is, the knowledge of the Chaturyugas - is that knowledge which combines numerous things constructed over past lives. It is at some juncture of such knowledge, divided into four eras, that a scholar or a layperson makes the determination of this knowledge. That juncture is called the celestial sphere (Nabhomandalam).

[GV3:P0054] Celestial spheres have nine natures. There is another nature that divides it into four. In which karma of self-knowledge called vision, and in which tendency can this nature be served to each person in different ways? The ability to impart the light of eras is the main thing here.

[GV3:P0055] The diverse historical truth of nine spheres is what is utilized in a soul. It cannot be illuminated by the glory of knowledge measured by the intellect. Then who can illuminate it? Passing through thousands of open spaces called 'the space is self-luminous', passing according to the changes in times, illuminating numerous earth spheres - the Guru who determines the worthiness of the course of dharma, and the disciple in whom that Guru's dharma resides. The karma that makes even a layperson or a scholar capable of asking what Kala Dharma is by convincing them of the epochal differences of Satya, Treta, Dwapara, and Kali - this is the compassion of the special path of dharma prepared jointly by this Guru and disciple.

[GV3:P0056] Guruvani

[GV3:P0057] Guru Jayanthi Edition September 1999

[GV3:P0058] The Tapas Practice Entitled to the Yuga Dharma

[GV3:P0059] There was a state when I tried to think about how my past life was. Crores of souls who took human form and reached the state of the Trimurtis stand in the subtle realm. All are form-concepts created by humans. That is, a conceptual form belonging to the artistic sense of an artist who draws outlines. The subtle realm is a procession of crores of conceptual forms that humans have imagined in this way. Rahu and Ketu are formed by the gathering of the light of such conceptual forms. This even covers the sun and the moon. That is how an eclipse occurs. During an eclipse, the rays of the sun hit the moon, and its dust particles falling on the earth are considered poisonous potencies. This is shown to ascetics. They will purify these toxic substances (mercury, sulfur, vermilion, etc.) found from the earth and keep them in their bodies. The practice of alchemy (Rasavada) is purifying and applying the most poisonous of these. Scientists say that even gold can be made from this. This is what is depicted as a peacock, the vehicle of Subramanya. It shines because it has more copper in it. The treatment method of applying peacock oil arose by applying intellect in this. An application of even greater intellect is the Kayakalpa treatment performed by ascetics. If Kayakalpa treatment is done, then food and water are not needed. The eight siddhis and Samadhi by bursting the head are all parts of this.

[GV3:P0060] When an ascetic who has performed Kalpa Seva is made to meditate sitting in a cave with eight faces, changing positions according to zodiacs and stars, the bones in the body will become like cotton, making him unable to stand or walk. Siddha medicine is a treatment system completed by consuming the Navapashanas (nine poisons) in various ways along with Guru Kalpa. The things done by creating caves with seven and nine faces and keeping the body at each cave entrance at every watch (Yama) are part of this treatment. It takes eighteen and a half years to complete this Kalpa Seva system by taking this body and placing it in all nine cave entrances as watches change and turn. The Puranas and Vedic sciences are descriptions of what was completed in this way. The six-faced Subramanya is the one who carried the Kalpa Seva as six sciences. His vehicle is the peacock. It is poison. Subramanya's body had the strength to carry this much poison. The authors of the Puranas called this Subramanya 'Mayilvahanan' (He who rides the peacock).

[GV3:P0061] The state of Subramanya is the power of penance acquired over numerous births. Names like Shubhramaniyan and Arumukhan came because of this. Vyasa, who devised this, was brought in, made a Vaishnava, given the name Krishnadwaipayana, and depicted. Characters like Drona, Bhishma, and Shalya are stories depicted by devising such imaginations. Shaivism, Shaktism, and Vaishnavism are also imaginations devised over various periods. What is described by differentiating this is Ravana's head. His head needs to be equal to the heads of ten Brahmins. That is, he has the intellect of ten Brahmins. That character was changed into a Brahmin, and changed into Ravana. Where he was supposed to attain ten states, he was made Ravana. He couldn't be devised into ten states, could he?

[GV3:P0062] It is by keeping aside the soul that grows like this that it incarnates as a Guru. It is by assigning this meaning that it is said a Brahmin should not be questioned. [GV3:P0317] God worship is practiced in all forms in any logic. That is, whichever devil is worshipped, we do it calling out 'Oh God'. God worship is knowledge done according to justice. This has been done for a long time.

[GV3:P0318] Whatever pains have come due to our birth, there is a reason for all of them. An effect will not occur without a reason. So knowing what that reason is, Santhigiri's way is saying how God worship should be done according to our capability and capacity. That shouldn't be done just suddenly either. Because we should respect whichever devil or god or whatever we respected and worshipped. And only after giving what needs to be given to it and moving it aside, should we do something else instead. You shouldn't think you can just do it like that. What is there to discard from it, what good is there to do for it, doing both of these, we will establish dharma for a karma we get by struggling with our life. We don't need siddhis or blessings or curses. We have nothing to get from that. The karma we take with pain, we live in a way that not only our countrymen but even our children cannot recognize it. You must consider it as a path given by God for recognition.

[GV3:P0319] Guru Vani

[GV3:P0320] Guru Jayanthi Edition

[GV3:P0321] September 1999

[GV3:P0322] Who will help us?

[GV3:P0323] The action of knowledge (Jnana Karma) is beyond intellect, beyond thought, and vast like the sky. What can the Puranas, epics, and scientific sense do when they give importance only to the intellect in such action? Even great thinkers and highly educated people are unable to evaluate and study their own lives. Without that ability, can love be sustained by merely talking about an extraordinary imaginative faculty?

[GV3:P0324] Intelligence, capability, and competence are indeed necessary to maintain the richness of love. But one can never evoke love by writing commentaries on the meanings of words using only intellect, capability, and competence. Such is the nature of scholars. However, we should not mistakenly perceive the life of a scholar. In the nature of karma, while trying to maintain education, wealth, and status, if there is a setback in protecting their pride, all their thoughts will be impaired. Moreover, by destroying all the goodness of life, they will try to seek spiritual merit by preaching, singing, and writing all the knowledge they have acquired to convince the world. This is about the biggest mistake among the blunders that befall those who get carried away by the vibration of education. Whenever such a soul is born, it always comes hidden behind the guise of scholarship. Most of them will neither be able to respect the dharma of the times nor seek self-acquired merit. By then, the soul would have become highly irritable, making it impossible for the capability of the learned intellect to merge through love. Instead, they will waste time finding faults in the Puranas using logic, Vedas, and epics. Later, even if they are afflicted with some kind of disease—and not an ordinary one—their scholarly pride will not leave them. When various diseases oppress and weaken them, if there is no one to offer an inquiring mind and luck stays completely far away, then they can do nothing. However, if the rigidity of the mind decreases in their final days by calling upon God, we can consider it as the merit of some past birth. Even then, they will only believe in the worldly rules they have learned and taught. They will dismiss everyone else with contempt as ignorant. They will simply be unable to impart love.

[GV3:P0325] Most of them will also reach a state where they are unable to fulfill their duties to their own children or wife. If one is a brahmachari or a sanyasi, after a lot of learning, they will end up in a situation of cursing this education. Even then, without ever seeing simplicity in their own minds, they cannot think for the goodness of life other than just sharing their education, wealth, and all subsequent aspects of life. Or even if they do think, having read, known, and learned everything, they will end up as scholars who perform the karma of a distressed human lifespan and become empty. Then, they find fulfillment—in the case of Hindus—by turning some chaff and waste into ash, smearing it on their bodies, adorning themselves with sandalwood paste and vermilion for decoration, and becoming those who explain the meaning of the divine name.

[GV3:P0326] Assigning a meaning to this divine name is done like this: When Shiva was in the cremation ground, to prevent ghosts from approaching, he smeared himself with cremation ashes, held a spear and trident, and guarded the cemetery. This is the story told by one group. The story told by another group is different. That is, taking Shiva and Vishnu together, they apply sandalwood paste in place of Vishnu and a vermilion dot inside it. This is the meaning of the name that has come to represent Shaivite, Shakta, and Vaishnavite! Hindu scholars assign other meanings to this as well. When similarity was attained in the father's seed and the mother's blood, the Vaishnava concept provided coolness, touching it as the seat of the mind and instilling love. When they get exhausted going after all this, some find another theory and seek refuge in it.

[GV3:P0327] Do not assume that any of this is being rejected. We have a familiarity with practicing and following whatever changes and transformations have occurred in any religious doctrine from ancient times. Other than this, what else do we have? The difficulty faced when encountering experienced people is also immense. Whether the karmic path acquired over many births exists or not, when the liberationist and the rationalist come with their acquired good thoughts, this experienced person drags them into a karma that suffocates and frustrates them.

[GV3:P0328] What kind of person is an experienced one? Those who have experienced yakshis, ghosts, madans, and mantramurthis with a very special devotion are also experienced people. They can also perform some miraculous deeds. There are some who have given experiences in the lineage of gods and goddesses and in the lineage of prophets. We might also experience things in the way they learned and experienced them. Seeing this as the truth, they will attach their lives to it and proceed. There is no shortage of people who discuss good deeds by telling and making others listen to the histories of great men as examples. After all, they have the experience of making others experience these things. There is also no shortage of karma where the mind itself is lost in the light of misfortune, unable to utilize it for liberation.

[GV3:P0329] If there are such flaws in everything, how will we understand the truth? There is only one correct path to state for this. Do not set out to just learn and understand. Even if it is little knowledge, we have many experiences of seeking the light of experience. We must understand all this and make a decision. Each item is a completion of the good and bad karmic paths seen in this world. Due to the variations in the habit of thinking, it merely appears changed and turned in different ways. Therefore, if my soul exists, by the grace of God, I will find a personality who knows the dharmas of the era and becomes a vessel for realization. Aurobindo is someone who found it that way. There is no other medium for this.

[GV3:P0330] In return for calling upon God for a long time, five gurus known as Kalantara Gurus (Gurus across time) will come, who correct things according to the times without mixing up the disembodied and the manifested. Only they will help us. The aforementioned decision is what makes us capable of seeking the path of these gurus.

[GV3:P0331] If we fail to understand our ignorance about the dharma of our era and the state of becoming like a headless person, unable to impart dharma while staring at the karma of direct inferences, we will rot and decay in a deep pit similar to or even harsher than the pit of meaning-interpretation where water stagnates and termites and insects fall and rot. There is no solace for this in the theories of scholars and the ignorant. Believe that the scholars and the ignorant, who explain the meaning of the non-existent word 'Maya' by attaching it behind nihilism, cannot find a solution to this.

[GV3:P0332] Only the Kalantara Guru, who seeks the meaning by exploring the action-domain (Karma Kanda) of the knowledge sheaths through the five senses, five elements, and five sheaths, can attain this. That guide will be a follower of the Yuga Dharma, discovering a long-term familiarity of seeing meanings by giving due greatness and respect to everything without rejecting anything.

[GV3:P0333] How can we understand such a person? It is not about recognizing them. It is something that comes to us through our long-term fortune. That is, the period determined as Satya Yuga, Treta Yuga, Dwapara Yuga, and Kali Yuga, where a life functioned together starting from tiny creatures to the five senses, five elements, and five sheaths—this is what is meant by 'long time' (Kaladeergham). Only such a great soul can explain this to us.

[GV3:P0334] We have had many scholars for a long time who speak about letters and their associated meanings. Similarly, there have been Kalantara Gurus who have spoken about devotion, yoga, karma, and knowledge. If we happen to get a birth during the times when such Kalantara Gurus are born, through our life, we will be able to discover the numerous souls standing with the dharma of the times, with our physical eyes and with inherent purity. It will also show us what these souls have attained in the five senses and the five elements. That fortune is obtained from an ideal and timely visionary whose presence comes into the experience of millions of people. A true Guru is one who points out that even for religious scholars and our predecessor renunciates who guided the time cycles of gods and goddesses, the dharma of liberation is of no use because they do not know the dharma of the time.

[GV3:P0335] The time cycle of gods and goddesses refers to the Treta Yuga and Dwapara Yuga. Sri Krishna is the one who was born at the end of the Dwapara Yuga. The author of the Gita, who was a wise man by birth, himself has spoken about this time cycle. We also have many karmic paths that have been believed upon knowing that. Krishna, standing as Arjuna's Guru, made great scholars and experienced people like Drona and Bhishma fight and win the eighteenth battle known as the Kurukshetra war. When it is said that even through such an Arjuna, due to the ignorance of the Shudra class and the scholarly dharma of the elite scholars, the Kalantara Guru path where Shudras, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Brahmins worked together could not be sustained, whom will we hold onto? How will we hold on? This should be our thought.

[GV3:P0336] Sri Krishna is not the supramental radiance. Aurobindo Ghosh has said that it is the overmind bringing the supramental radiance into the land of temporal dharma. What should we see here? Only if we get an opportunity to be born, grow, and be nurtured during the period when a Dharma Guru is born, will we be able to understand the essence of the Yuga Dharma that has evolved over four eras. If we do not get a great soul who has attained the temporal dharma to be born into that karmic path, then we will never get the opportunity to discover this meaning.

[GV3:P0337] When we look at the many Gurus who came and went, like Buddha, like many other Gurus who sought only the truth, and like the prophets who knew the subtlety of the celestial dharma, we must also consider at this juncture that even they had to return without being able to find this essence.

[GV3:P0338] Guruvani

[GV3:P0339] Guru Jayanti Edition

[GV3:P0340] September 1999

[GV3:P0341] Our Tradition is an Unbearable Burden

[GV3:P0342] You might have some part of faith in you. But one should handle faith only after knowing its cause and effect. I am talking from my own experience. If someone suddenly jumps in and shows a siddhi (supernatural power), like blessing and cursing everything away, nothing will come of it, and nothing is going to happen here. People have some fake tricks in their hands like siddhis, illusions, and blessings. If one blesses and sends using such fake tricks, the prosperity of the house will only be lost. Moreover, when the children grow up, they will grow into utter wickedness.

[GV3:P0343] What is our need today? We have a karma that we have been doing until this very moment today. That karma has purity, it has a truth, it has everything. Do this only after knowing it. Do not just blindly believe it because someone says so. That is not right. God Himself will give us the knowledge and experience to achieve this. We should not throw away what God gives us. Whatever God gives is useful for all of you.

[GV3:P0344] Whoever you are, you are people who have lived based on a belief. This is not about any particular religion or caste. When that belief went astray in some way, religious doctrines came in and further distorted, preached, and propagated it—thus, the karmic path of that doctrine also became unknown. Each of us is the remainder of such an outdated karma. No one should assume that it will be fixed immediately. The hardships of some people, according to their willingness to suffer, will gradually reduce and then suddenly decrease. Then, where a huge destruction was supposed to happen, maybe just a finger will get cut. That is not to be considered a big deal. For example, instead of a severe fever, a mild fever and cough that puts one in bed for four days will come. At that time, you shouldn't say, "Oh, trouble has come, I am very distressed," this is not what should be said; all these are bound to happen. And it will pass on its own way.

[GV3:P0345] Our subject is this - how will this old karmic path of ours end, how should it be ended? If someone says that this karmic path, which I and my ancestors have spoken, practiced, done, and made others do until today, does not exist, it will not end. To say it will just end like that is foolishness. Wherever and whatever we have been doing, it will not end suddenly. But we have God's grace. A permanent solution for that old karma which we have been doing knowingly or unknowingly until today. That solution, the solution God shows us. That solution will not come unless the men, women, young, and old in the house strive together equally. If someone says God has come to stay extra with him, what can be done for that house? We can only tell the extra God to leave.

[GV3:P0346] Whether educated or uneducated, foolish or intelligent, capable or incapable, if everyone sees that God's greatness is one—if someone becomes arrogant thinking he has a lot of intelligence, we can only let it go its way. Nothing will come or go by being arrogant like that. If they become arrogant with education and wealth, let them be arrogant.

[GV3:P0347] Each of us is the remnant of the ignorance that says, "God is rooted in my caste, God is rooted in my religion." That is, we are standing on the wrong side of knowledge. If one thinks, "Some great soul has taken away all my mistakes and the shortcomings arising from them, now I just have to sit idly," things will not work out. This mistake is not something that any great soul can just wash away.

[GV3:P0348] As far as we are concerned, the karmic defect, or the quality of karma that has occurred through origin by birth - we must first come to the knowledge to experience this. Know and experience. Let the sorrow that is bound to come, come. Still, I must overcome it. This should be our goal. Saying, "Oh, I went there, everything is destined," is not knowledge. If you act upon such knowledge, unimaginable ruin will come to you. No matter how much it hurts or how much we struggle, we have to handle and overcome this.

[GV3:P0349] How will we know what our ancestors have done? If we say wealth and aristocracy should come equally to everyone, it is something that will not happen anywhere in the world. As part of giving wealth to everyone, someone in the past proposed giving thirteen and a half cents of land to each person. In the past, one person got thirteen and a half cents. How many people are there today? In the future, how many will there be? This is a trick to deceive these poor people. Another group will say, "I am struggling with work." What work? Whose work? For what? What if one works for the public good? What is public good? Let each one think. The house of the one who struggles will be ruined, that's it. Some clever ones will say, "Struggled a lot, couldn't know what love is." So, these things shouldn't just be said and compromised with.

[GV3:P0350] We will only receive what we are meant to get from the karma we painstakingly build with love, humility, and respect. Without love, without guidance, if someone says something and we decide to just jump into it, we will only jump. Nothing will be gained from there. Things will only happen according to the dynamics of the soul. If we say we have everything but cannot swallow a drop of water, isn't that the misfortune of the soul? Others have so many things in their hands to do for us. No one is doing anything. What to do? Will it be enough for us if someone gives us something for a day or ten days? Don't our children need to grow up? We must understand that none of this is a karma of a sense of justice. One can fabricate and say many things about the sense of justice. Destinies can be declared. But that is not the destiny of his soul. Regarding this destiny, both men and women are the same. If anyone says it is not so, it is guidance that pushes one entirely into alienation.

[GV3:P0351] We see various kinds of politicians. We see various kinds of religious theorists. Is anything they say actually happening here? Does anyone need to talk about the world? It is neither the fault of those who said this, nor the fault of those who knowingly repeated what was said. Without understanding the sorrows, knowledge, experience, and depth of its past and future, just jumping in and saying something will not accomplish anything. It hasn't worked to this day either. When we have so much evidence in front of us, why are we saying and showing all these unnecessary things? Anyone making you listen to such things is unnecessary.

[GV3:P0352] You all know that I am someone who has suffered a lot just like you. But I do not think about that suffering. If I think like that, can I live? It is true, there was suffering, that is its nature. God gave a dignity to that suffering. If God gives us, we should be willing to share it with everyone. That is sacrifice. For that, money, capability, wealth, everything will be needed.

[GV3:P0353] What is the reason for our suffering? It is the unbearable burden of our tradition. What is that burden? Our soul's lack of dharma, lack of luck, lack of merit. Can one just go somewhere one day, throw it away, and come back? Do not say such things to anyone. What is being said is not right. These are all deceptive tricks of religious doctrines, siddhi justifications, and miraculous deeds meant to fool people. No one should ever believe these.

[GV3:P0354] As for us, we have God's mercy. What is being said is the truth. But one must feel the pain for God's mercy. We might not know anything about such things. But one thing, when we finish doing good and bad deeds, we go again and perform karma according to the rules of the respective religion. And then jump around in the logic of the non-believer. Whatever anyone else does, what is it to you? That is not what I am saying. None of us should think that we can improve by acting otherwise. It is the father's fault, it is the mother's fault, it is the land's fault, it is the country's fault—what is all this? The land we were born in lacks luck. What is the reason for us being born in that place? Isn't it enough to see that we are even unluckier than that?

[GV3:P0355] Yes, we are worse than everything else. Our ancestors were those who, enveloped in a huge cover of loveless actions without ever knowing what the dynamics of the soul are, danced towards destruction thinking it was love. When God gives us an opportunity to change from this, you—father, mother, husband, and wife—should never behave leaving it aside. Only then can you be saved. If you leave it, you will never be set right.

[GV3:P0356] All this is a karma that can occur if we are born. If we reject all this and walk away, our dharma or karma does not become complete. Only if you do it with effort, keep a detached mind to know and remove the sins and merits that have come due to the ignorance of the ancestors, and tie love and respect along with it, will you be able to remove it. Otherwise, you will never remove it. After a while, you will abandon your faith and leave. This is a familiar experience of mine.

[GV3:P0357] Let our past theories be right or wrong. We do not need to try fixing them by debating their rights and wrongs. We were born. Now, what all can we do for this? Let us think about a time when God showed us some mercy as an opportunity for this. A karmic path for us to know each other, speak, do, and make others do. That should be a love that comes towards dharma. It should not be a love where merit is lost. Destruction will happen there. In this matter, you should act with strong determination. If God gives us an opportunity to do it and make others do it systematically, it must be done. That persistence—that love and respect—must be held onto without letting go. If it goes without love, humility, and respect, everything will follow that absence. Most of our ancestors were those who went that way. We shouldn't jump around seeing that. If some miraculous deeds are shown, or the full form of siddhi paths are shown, none of it will be of use to us. We shouldn't believe in any such thing. Our love will cease to exist. Understanding this much, you must strive hard. If you waste time, you must strive hard. Otherwise, time will be lost. How many people do we see in front of us who have lost their time and opportunities like this? Some will do many things unable to bear it out of love. After a while, all their love is gone. Did a thief take it? This is all I have to say. I cannot bring you closer by talking about other things. Depending on your knowledge and love, it can be taken.

[GV3:P0358] Regarding knowledge, I do not intend to thrust great knowledge upon you. Your knowledge is less, your experience is less, your familiarity is less. You don't even know what the sins and merits of your ancestors are. Let it be whatever it is. I happened to be born, happened to grow up. Or else, something will happen in this life. Let whatever happen. I need a liberation from this. That liberation should pave the way to salvation (Mukti). This should be our thought. Rather than that, there is no point in us getting agitated and jumping around hearing whatever anyone says.

[GV3:P0359] Many have fallen because they did not do this knowingly. Therefore, this matter is being told straight to you. I have seen my experience to be like that. If there is knowledge in that direction, we won't face any unseemly situations. We can do whatever can be lifted up with our own love, respect, and humility.

[GV3:P0360] You will experience diseases, sorrows, difficulties, and poverty in many forms. This is present in all human beings. Some do not get cured even if treated. When treated for some, another disease comes. Another one is an incurable disease. Even though we say many things as reasons for this, it is the soul's lack of merit. What can be done to cure the soul's lack of merit? It reaches a state where it cannot be grasped in any way. Even if we ask those who come as great believers and great visionaries, there is no solution. It is difficult to find such a person.

[GV3:P0361] This difficulty is the same among Hindus, Christians, Buddhists, and Jains. Because, we celebrate a familiar practice we followed for a long time. When such a concept is continuously imparted, this karma becomes like a disease and a sorrow. It happens to many people like that. Nobody says what the reason for this coming is. The method of most people is to believe in whatever any of our ancestors worshipped, and occasionally go and pray. But do not assume that this will become worship of God. Worship of God means we can do it in every way; the concept is that God is in everything. It is not like that. Regarding what is called God, this concept has emerged due to the numerous mistakes made because we did not do it and understand it according to each era. It has not come because of any other shortcoming.

[GV3:P0362] Many people who lived in grand ways, and that too those who lived doing many good deeds, are caught in such a concept. If it is said that the reason for all this is the soul lacking merit, will wealth and capability come to those without any merit? But how should that merit be used, in what way should it be done so that it remains as merit, what should our life turn it into—we have not learned any of this. If a little wealth or capability comes, we should live grandly, look down slightly on others, and through them, we should become big. This is what is learned. What merit does the soul have for us with this mindset? We have a past experience of living like this for crores of births. How can this be changed?

[GV3:P0363] Some fall very far behind in purity of character. However, some who have a little capability, skill, and respect will carry it around as a great status and completely destroy even the merit they possess. This is an artificial construct among us.

[GV3:P0364] We will live, grow, and die. What good is there for our soul? We carry around this foul-smelling body by scrubbing and bathing it. If the soul is not in this body, what will we do? If such a soul becomes like a rotten tree, what will we do? No one comes forward to say how this should be resolved. When we suffer the most, where will we go? To some astrologer, or a sorcerer, or some temple, or if some Swami is sitting somewhere, then there. No one should assume that we will get merit from these places. That assumption is not special. What is the deficiency in our soul - this is the target. How can this deficiency of the soul be changed - we do not know this at all.

[GV3:P0365] What we have heard is the Trinity system, or the Prophetic system, or the path of the Guru—let it be anything, can we only go the way the word of God is received? If we go through this path, after four thousand or five thousand years, what will we be able to know about our ancestors? If we go according to the calculation of ages (Yugas), crores of matters come up according to the calculation of ages. Can we go knowing all this?

[GV3:P0366] No tradition has ever taught us according to the Yuga Dharma (duty of the age). This is the reason for the shortcomings of all people. Can we immediately live according to this Yuga Dharma? No. But this is the time destined for it.

[GV3:P0367] Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra—this much is stated as Varna Dharma (duty based on class). It hasn't been said whose Yuga Dharma this is for which time. Because it is taught that the Dharma of Kali (Yuga) is bad, there are people who believe that none of this should be done in this Kali Yuga. It is not like that; if this Kali is entirely meant for the Shudra, then this Shudra has the authority. That is, Kali is the time when the Shudra is entitled to Brahma Jnana (knowledge of Brahman). He can achieve it only in Kali. We must firmly establish a belief that through the Dharma of Kali, the Shudra can acquire the authority for Brahma Jnana. Otherwise, no matter which politics is spoken, which caste is spoken, or which religion is spoken, our sorrow will not be alleviated. A deficiency that ancestors followed and worshipped, regardless of which sphere they belonged to, exists for all families that have aged in life. Thinking that there is no oldness is also our ignorance.

[GV3:P0368] There are many people who worship tiny gods for tiny castes and live in forests and beaches. They will not have any knowledge about what God is. When they do things based on what they have heard and seen here and there, everything will go out of rhythm. Eventually, he will die and go stand somewhere. If one dies, one shouldn't assume the soul is saved. Wherever there is life that has happened with complete ignorance, it will go and stand there.

[GV3:P0369] Everyone knows that there is a sky around this earth. Beyond the layer of the earth, there are three visible exteriors - Earth, Moon, and Sun. Between these, some spheres that cannot be seen by the eye are moving. These are called Navajyothis. Or else it can be called sky or earth. There is such a calculation. Can one operate knowing all these calculations? You don't need to know any of that. All this certainly exists. Meaning, there is no need to wait to know all this before proceeding. It is impossible to go having known it like that.

[GV3:P0370] I will tell you some things that you can do. When we consistently do something, the mind will go downwards. This is some deficiency of the soul. As we grow, we will act in various ways. What if a disease comes at that time? This is the soul's lack of merit. We are also unable to generate merit for this soul. This is the shortcoming of us human race. An astrologer will look and tell you to do this and that. Doing that won't make a difference.

[GV3:P0371] Our ancestors who lived have become devas (gods), devis (goddesses), rishis, sanyasis, or jnanis. Where do all these stand as dead ties? Coming as their successors and dying, billions of souls are standing in zodiacs without merit. Then the children born become sickly, when they grow up they don't get what they need for their growth, they lack the ability to work and achieve—this is usually called family curse (Kudumba Dosham). But this is not just a family curse, it is also a deficiency of the soul. This must be corrected through life.

[GV3:P0372] Sri Krishna is the one who came as the greatest person. How did we perceive what Krishna said? Krishna came as a jnani (wise one) by birth. No one else came as a jnani by birth. They become jnanis after coming. Not only that, by birth and origin, he was a person born after passing the position of a deva. That is why Krishna got the dark color. Sri Krishna's color is the color of the sky. Does the sky actually have a color? No. He attained a state and came as a Guru. That is how he defeated his uncles and ancestors like Drona and Bhishma in archery. Why kill them? The ancestors (Pitrus) they killed stand elsewhere. If these Pitrus continue to stand like this, if they remain alive, this war cannot be won. Therefore, he just killed them. He got Arjuna to kill them. This should be understood in this way.

[GV3:P0373] We have learned that Sri Krishna is the greatest. Not just learned, it is an experience. What is known about Sri Krishna is that he is a Jnani. Being a Jnani means having no attachment to father, mother, husband, children, or anything. But there is a connection—with the truth. This is Sri Krishna. Didn't he kill his children? That is Sri Krishna's quality. Without understanding Krishna in this way, we have learned the story of sixteen thousand and eight women. In the very place where we worshipped the Deva and Devi, we are worshipping Krishna as well. This is our mistake. Sri Krishna is not such a person.

[GV3:P0374] The Gopa women are those who accepted only Krishna as their Guru over many births. What is meant by sixteen thousand and eight? It is a scene in the eighth state. If Sri Krishna's soul leaves the body, then it can stand taking a form, stand without a form - and it can also scatter as atoms. That is Sri Krishna. Because we did not get the knowledge to see Sri Krishna this way, what did we do? Along with worshipping Devas and Devis, our ancestors worshipped Krishna too.

[GV3:P0375] Even though Krishna came freely in this manner, his uncles could not see that greatness. Therefore, even before Sri Krishna was born, how much sorrow that family experienced!

[GV3:P0376] When we say a mother, that mother will get happiness and sorrow from her children. If they fall into such a karma, that mother should become complete through that life. Not by rejecting husband, wife, and children, but by properly following the practices related to them. One shouldn't do anything by abandoning children, abandoning father, abandoning mother, or abandoning husband. Through our life, we are living out a life.

[GV3:P0380] The Soul that is Set Aside

[GV3:P0384] What is the difference between a ghost, a Deva, and a human? Regarding the ghost, besides what is mentioned in Puranas and epics, there are many types of ghosts. At the same time, there are demonic karmas that pass with time. Like building a bridge without deciding the location, or like those who take contracts desiring profit. It doesn't mean profit is not needed. For a fish market vendor, he will only get a crore in profit if he sells to lakhs of people. The knowledge, experience, and habit of a wholesale merchant who collects and supplies goods according to the season is not the same as someone who takes and supplies goods day by day. The wholesale merchant looks at the pros and cons, calculates that an item will barely last this long, or seeing that it is something that will be lost, if it is an unusable item, he will sell it off before its time expires, by reducing or increasing the price. But a retail vendor cannot do any of this. Just as he can only do with what he has, followers of Yuga Dharmas have certain tasks that they resolve in the soul over a Yuga. Through the Satya Yuga, there are those who live, perform karma, and attain a true form according to their respective tendencies. That accumulation of form takes ages, and is executed after seeing the beginning, middle, and end forms in the meaning of a Yuga Dharma. Like a woodcutter standing in a forest or village in the beginning, bringing the cut wood to the place he intends, experiencing the difficulty of not having discovered iron or similar materials of that kind, struggling, he will somehow complete that task. When iron cannot be used to cut a dry tree in the forest, he will pluck wild vines suitable for cutting it, tie it and pull it to one side, and do whatever he can to take it to the place he intends. That karma performer knows how to bring it to some tree or level ground and process it the way it needs to be done. Similarly, he will also discover some techniques finding that each wood has a specific quality. Thus, he will perform all form-resolutions concerning the wood.

[GV3:P0385] What is form-resolution? Like the growth of the mind and the thinking habit of knowledge, using that wood, he will craft the forms intended in his mind through a special power of imagination. Because, in that era, iron or other tools had not been discovered to cut and unfold them into forms, right? By the time he reaches the next Yuga, he would have sat and thought about this many times, wondering what the solution for this is. It can be seen that this is a karmic path where his own births change into many forms.

[GV3:P0386] Like someone thinking about the theory of evolution, like someone discovering tools and understanding their use and nature over time, there were some great souls who sought merit through births in every subject.
